En 1889, Svante Arrhenius relie la vites: In 1889, Svante Arrhenius linked reaction speed to an "activation energy" that molecules must overcome. The colder it is, the fewer manage it.
Fermier général, Lavoisier est guillotin: A tax farmer, Lavoisier was guillotined on 8 May 1794. Lagrange: "It took them only an instant to cut off this head, and a hundred years might not suffice to reproduce its like."
Le 20 mars 1800, Alessandro Volta décrit: On 20 March 1800, Alessandro Volta described to the Royal Society his pile of copper and zinc discs separated by cardboard soaked in salt water. He had been inspired by Luigi Galvani's frog legs.
La glace carbonique est observée pour la: Dry ice was first observed in 1835 by the Frenchman Adrien-Jean-Pierre Thilorier. The English name "dry ice" was trademarked in 1925.
L'échelle d'Anders Celsius, en 1742, éta: Anders Celsius's 1742 scale was upside down: 0 for boiling water, 100 for ice. Linnaeus flipped it in 1745, a year after his death.
En 1761, l'Écossais Joseph Black compren: In 1761, the Scot Joseph Black realised that heat given to melting ice goes into changing its state, not raising its temperature: "latent heat".
Boyle doit sa loi à une pompe à vide per: Boyle owed his law to a vacuum pump improved with Robert Hooke's help. Henry Power had formulated the hypothesis in 1661, and Boyle cited it in 1662, mistakenly crediting Richard Towneley.
Le mot « plasma » est introduit en 1928: The word "plasma" was introduced in 1928 by American chemist Irving Langmuir, probably by analogy with blood plasma, which carries particles.
L'azote est liquéfié pour la première fo: Nitrogen was first liquefied on 15 April 1883 at the Jagiellonian University in Kraków, by Polish physicists Zygmunt Wróblewski and Karol Olszewski.
Van Helmont emploie le mot « gaz » dans: Van Helmont used the word "gas" in his 1652 Ortus medicinae. He wrote that he had chosen it as "not far from chaos", the Greek word.
Berzelius est le premier à distinguer le: Berzelius was the first to distinguish organic compounds, which contain carbon, from inorganic ones. He also gave us the words "protein" (1838) and "polymer" (1833).
Les historiens nuancent ce récit : Wöhle: Historians qualify this story: Wöhler was no crusader against the vital force, and the idea was already in retreat. A 2000 survey found this "Wöhler myth" in 90% of chemistry textbooks.
En 1920, Hermann Staudinger propose que: In 1920, Hermann Staudinger proposed that rubber, starch and proteins are very long chains. Almost all his colleagues rejected the idea; he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1953.
En 1897, Eduard Buchner fait fermenter d: In 1897, Eduard Buchner fermented sugar with mere juice from crushed yeast, without living cells: fermentation is due to enzymes. Nobel Prize 1907.
En 1797, Smithson Tennant brûle diamant: In 1797, Smithson Tennant burned diamond and graphite and obtained the same amount of gas: they are two forms of the same element.
Wallace Carothers se suicide en avril 19: Wallace Carothers took his own life in April 1937, sixteen months before nylon was publicly announced. He never saw his invention go on sale.
Kekulé dit en 1890 que l'idée du cycle d: In 1890 Kekulé said the idea of the benzene ring came to him in a daydream of a snake biting its own tail. Some historians suspect the story was made up.
Avant la bakélite, le Belge Leo Baekelan: Before Bakelite, the Belgian Leo Baekeland had made his fortune with Velox, the first commercially successful photographic paper: his company was bought in 1899 by George Eastman of Kodak for $750,000.
Une étude de la NOAA prédit dès 1988 une: A NOAA paper predicted as early as 1988 a zone where plastic would accumulate in the North Pacific. Sailor Charles Moore crossed it in 1997 and made it known.
Le 27 août 1859, près de Titusville en P: On 27 August 1859, near Titusville, Pennsylvania, Edwin Drake's well struck oil at 21 metres: the first commercial oil well in the United States.
Louis Camille Maillard décrit en 1912 la: Louis Camille Maillard described the reaction between sugars and amino acids in 1912. He died in Paris in 1936.
Les plus anciennes traces de fabrication: The oldest traces of soap-like materials come from Babylon, around 2800 BC. Pliny the Elder credited soap to the Gauls.
Le chlore est étudié en 1774 par Scheele: Chlorine was studied in 1774 by Scheele, and Humphry Davy named it in 1810 from the Greek for "pale green". It was used as a chemical weapon from 1915, in the First World War.
Des tablettes sumériennes et le papyrus: Sumerian tablets and the Ebers papyrus already mention willow. In 1897, at Bayer, Felix Hoffmann (or perhaps Arthur Eichengrün) obtained pure acetylsalicylic acid; the name Aspirin dates from 1899.
La première pile, celle de Volta, est dé: The first battery, Volta's, was described in 1800. It came out of a dispute: Luigi Galvani thought the frog produced the electricity, Volta that it came from the two metals.
Le PTFE découvert par Roy Plunkett en 19: The PTFE discovered by Roy Plunkett in 1938 took the trade name Teflon in 1945. Heat-resistant and inert, it is also used to insulate cables and coat medical implants.
Le ciment Portland est breveté par l'Ang: Portland cement was patented by the Englishman Joseph Aspdin in 1824, and reinforced concrete invented by Joseph Monier in 1849. The Romans already used concrete widely: the Pantheon's dome is the largest in unreinforced concrete.
Les feux d'artifice sont nés en Chine, s: Fireworks were born in China, under the Song dynasty (960-1279). Modern bright colours come from chlorate chemistry: in 1786, Berthollet observed the violet flame of potassium chlorate.
Becquerel avait rangé ses plaques et ses: Becquerel had stored his plates and uranium salts in a drawer on 26 and 27 February 1896, for lack of sun. On 1 March, the plates were fogged anyway. He shared the 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie.
La notion de demi-vie vient d'Ernest Rut: The idea of half-life comes from Ernest Rutherford, in 1907, who used it to date rocks. The term "half-life" took hold in the early 1950s.
La datation au carbone 14 est mise au po: Carbon-14 dating was developed in 1949 by Willard Libby at the University of Chicago, tested on sequoias of known age from their rings. Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1960.
Le mot « isotope », « même place » en gr: The word "isotope", Greek for "same place", was suggested to Frederick Soddy in 1913 by the physician Margaret Todd. Why isotopes differ was only understood in 1932, with the neutron.
Lise Meitner, qui avait dû fuir l'Allema: Lise Meitner, who had had to flee Nazi Germany in July 1938, explained fission with her nephew Otto Frisch at Christmas 1938. The 1944 Nobel went to Otto Hahn alone; element 109 now bears her name, meitnerium.
En 1938-1939, Hans Bethe explique commen: In 1938-1939, Hans Bethe explained how stars shine through fusion reactions, first for the Sun with Charles Critchfield. Nobel Prize in Physics 1967.
Marie Curie est la première femme à rece: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel, and one of only two people awarded in two fields, with Linus Pauling. Her notebooks, still radioactive, are kept in lead-lined boxes.
Le becquerel est adopté comme unité offi: The becquerel was adopted as an official unit in 1975, replacing the curie, a unit based on the activity of one gram of radium.
C'est Rutherford qui, en 1899, distingue: It was Rutherford who, in 1899, distinguished alpha and beta rays by their penetrating power. In 1909, with Thomas Royds, he showed that alpha particles are helium nuclei.
Il faut près de deux ans à Grace Fryer e: It took Grace Fryer and four colleagues about two years to find a lawyer. The case opened in January 1928 and settled that autumn: $10,000 each and a lifetime annuity.
Ce jour-là, Arthur Compton prévient Jame: That day, Arthur Compton told James Conant in code: "The Italian navigator has landed in the New World." Eugene Wigner brought out a bottle of Chianti, drunk from paper cups.
